newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approves U.S. news organizations for Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approves U.S. news organizations for Cuba.

text.p: The White House announced on Wednesday that the United States has approved licenses for 10 American media organisations to open news bureaus in Cuba.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the decision was in keeping with President Bill Clinton's stated policy to support an "increased flow of accurate information to and from and within Cuba itself."

"The administration believes that news gathering and reporting by U.S. news organisations will keep international attention focused on the situation in Cuba and the realities of economic and political conditions there and will bring greater public exposure to those who are advocating a democratic change in Cuba," McCurry told reporters.

Licenses were granted to television networks CNN, CBS and ABC, the Associated Press wire service, newspapers the Miami Herald, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel and the Chicago Tribune, the news agency and newspaper group Dow Jones, and the Spanish-language television network Univision.
A license also went to CubaINFO, a newsletter associated with the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies.
All but CNN must seek approval from the Cuban government to set up operations in Havana. CNN already obtained Cuban approval.
